chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Shorty Baker learns to read in Redman's band
summary: Redman found Harold Baker in St. Louis in 1936 and taught him to read; working with Redman was like school.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: And Shorty Baker, Harold Baker. I worked with him in Don Redman's band. In fact, we took him away from St. Louis in 1936. Don picked him up. He was a slow reader and Don taught him how to read. Like I told you, it was the same as going to school when you worked with Don.

Yeah. He would take you and teach you what you didn't know. I've seen him take saxophone players, and you have a tough passage, he'd look at the way you was fingering and he'd take the saxophone away from you and show you how to finger it to make it easier for you.
And Shorty Baker was a great trumpet
player in that band, to me.
